thread:
Jonah: hi team, Jonah here. first week trying to build runtime from source. build fails at link with undefined references to cuBLASLt symbols and ldd on the .so shows libcuda.so.1 => /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so.1 (0x...) but runtime still errors at load due to 'cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory' when running the unit tests. any tips for rpath/ldconfig issues?

Priya: welcome! quick guess — your container image might include CUDA toolkit libs in /usr/local/cuda but the host driver libs are elsewhere. Are you running the tests inside the same container that was built or in a minimal runtime image? also paste the exact lderror.

Jonah: running tests inside the build image. error when running pytest: 
```
OSError: /workspace/build/libinfruntime.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```
but `ldd build/libinfruntime.so` shows many libs found and libcuda resolved to /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so.1.

Sato: that can happen if RUNPATH isn't set or the loader can't follow the symlink. do `readelf -d build/libinfruntime.so | grep RUNPATH` and `readlink -f /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so.1`

Jonah: readelf output: `0x000000000000001d (RUNPATH) Library runpath: [$ORIGIN/../lib:/usr/local/lib]` and readlink gives `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1` (the file inside host). so the binary expects CUDA in /usr/local/cuda but libcuda is actually a host path. weird.

Priya: aha — mismatch between where the build put the CUDA toolkit and where the host driver libs are mounted. Two approaches: (1) during docker run, bind the host lib dir to /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu and add that to LD_LIBRARY_PATH, or (2) patch the built .so RUNPATH to include the host path using patchelf. We usually prefer 1 for CI.

Hannah: adding to note — avoid shipping full CUDA toolkit inside final runtime image. It confuses rpath and can cause tests to pick up incompatible libcuda. Our internal build pattern: compile in image with toolkit but when running tests we start a thin runtime image that mounts host driver libs to /host-drivers and sets `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/host-drivers:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.

Jonah: tried bind-mounting host /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu into /host-drivers and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/host-drivers` before running tests — that fixed the pytest OSError, but now I get unresolved cuBLASLt symbols at runtime even though the static link step succeeded.

Sato: unresolved at runtime -> probably different lib order or version mismatch. run `nm -D /host-drivers/libcublasLt.so | grep cublasLt` and compare sonames: `objdump -p /host-drivers/libcublasLt.so | grep SONAME` vs your linked lib's `ldd`. Also check `strings /host-drivers/libcuda.so.1 | grep 535` to confirm driver version.

Jonah: good call. host driver is 535.x, but the libcublasLt in /usr/local/cuda was from toolkit 12.0. replaced by host /host-drivers version and reran — now tests pass locally.

Priya: for CI, add a small preflight step in the build matrix to ensure runtime image doesn't include toolkit libs or to remap them. Example snippet we use in CI (bash):
```bash
# fail fast if runtime image contains toolkit libs
if docker run --rm my-runtime:ci bash -lc "ls /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcublasLt.so >/dev/null 2>&1"; then
  echo 'ERROR: runtime image contains CUDA toolkit libs, mount host drivers instead' >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

infra-bot: CI: job runtime-build (commit abc123) failed preflight — runtime image contained toolkit libs.

Jonah: thanks everyone, learned a lot about rpath vs host lib mounting. i'll update my Dockerfile to separate build/runtime stages and add the CI check. super helpful :pray:
